segments.text: A torpedo sinks his ship in two minutes. Then he drifts alone on a raft for {133|a hundred and thirty-three} days. And he lives.
No chance. Nobody lasts four months out there. Let's go look.
November {1942|nineteen forty-two}. Poon Lim is a steward on a British cargo ship. Two torpedoes hit. He jumps. Two hours later, he finds an empty raft.
Eight feet square. Some biscuits, some water. Then nothing.
So he bends a flashlight spring into a fish hook. Rope becomes line. A tin becomes a knife. Rain becomes water.
He catches seabirds. Then a shark.
A freighter passes. It does not stop. Navy planes spot him. Then a storm hides him.
Day {133|one thirty-three}. Three fishermen find him off Brazil. He has lost just twenty pounds.
Still the record for one person alone on a raft. I was wrong. Case closed.
